chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Chick Webb's last talk at Keyes Restaurant
summary: On the final trip, Webb asked McRae to take care of the band and Ella.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

in front of Keyes Restaurant and we was talking on the Cadillac (inaudible) back of this (inaudible). His wife was setting in the car.
And she wasn't (nothing inaudible). He was talking to me -- he talked as long as he wanted. He said, 'What I want you to do for me now, if you don't never see me' --
(inaudible), 'Look, if this thing don't turn out right, do me one favor. Take care of the band. Take care of Ella.'
'Don't let the guys mess up, just take care of Ella,' you know. (inaudible).
I say, 'Ah, man, come on, you're going to be all right. You know, everything's going to be all right.'

He say, 'Nah, (inaudible).' I call it downtown. I go downtown and take care of his business (inaudible) -- kidding with me on that. 'Take care of Ella (inaudible). I don't know how the thing going to turn out.'
